name: Wales

changes.why: The FAW gave the senior men's and women's teams equal match fees from January 2023 (part-funded by a 25% cut to the men's fees), covering up to the 2026 men's and 2027 women's World Cups; this was not in the earlier evidence and matches the +0.2 given to Denmark and the equal-pay credit given to the Netherlands.

missing_checked: no current betting partner: past deals with Dafabet (2015-18) and BOB Sports (Asian-market betting brand, global partner from May 2021 on a three-year deal) have ended; partners listed on faw.cymru in Jan 2026 are EE, Admiral (insurance), McDonald's, Sport Wales, plus JD and Adidas (no 2024+ renewal of BOB Sports found; marked as not found, not proven absent)
no UEFA/FIFA discrimination or violence sanctions on the FAW 2021-26 found (last fan-conduct fines are from 2014 and earlier)
governance: CEO Noel Mooney extended to 2030 (Jan 2026), governance reform programme, Cymru Football Foundation nearly GBP 30m to grassroots facilities; no scandal 2025-26, O stays 7
coach: Bellamy stayed after a reported Burnley move collapsed (June 2026); no churn
government: UK Free (Freedom House 92), no hard line
notes: Equal-pay deal runs to the 2027 Women's World Cup; no extension beyond that found yet. Jess Fishlock criticised the FAW's pay commitment in an S4C documentary (undated, probably before the 2023 deal); not counted. With both changes in this batch Wales (V 8.2) moves further ahead of Norway (V 7.5) for 3rd place.

name: Norway

changes.why: Verified: Norsk Tipping (the state-owned gaming monopoly, which runs Oddsen sports betting and online casino as well as lotteries) renewed in March 2026 as general partner of the NFF for 2026-2029, covering the men's and women's national teams plus Eliteserien and Toppserien. That is a top-tier betting sponsor, so the Denmark yardstick applies (-0.8); no ad limits like Denmark's were found, but the brand is the lottery-led company rather than a betting-only brand and its surplus goes to sport by law, so it is not worse than Denmark.

missing_checked: FIFA fined the NFF CHF 10,000 (Nov 2025) for anthem disturbance, a pitch invader and order/security at the Oct 2025 Israel qualifier in Oslo; not discrimination, no flags charged; treated as minor and not counted (as Scotland's 2021 anthem fine was)
no UEFA discrimination or violence sanctions on the NFF 2021-26 found
NFF under Klaveness kept its stance (Israel-match profits to Doctors Without Borders Gaza work, July 2026 call to suspend Israel per FIFA rules); already in the V evidence, no further change
women's equal pay since 2017 already counted
government: Free (Freedom House 99, RSF 1st), no hard line; Norsk Tipping is state-owned but a domestic gaming monopoly, not a state-backing case
notes: Round 1 flagged Norsk Tipping as unverified; it is now verified as the NFF's general partner to 2029 (fee not disclosed; one trade report says lower than the 2021 deal of NOK 258m, unverified). If Kevin sees a state lottery-led monopoly as milder than Denmark's Oddset brand, -0.4 (V 7.9) is the lower bound, the same range given for Denmark. The previous research's own note said 'lower V by 1 if a main partner'; -0.8 is used for consistency with Denmark. Effect: Norway's gap to Wales for 3rd in the Nations League grows (Norway was 0.6 behind).
